name: Gog East Face
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier.
[approach] Gog is the higher, closer-to-the-col summit of the Gog-Magog pair, and the route starts on its east face, reached by hiking across the snow below it and crossing the moat to the rock.
[descent_text] Cross the moat and walk down the snowfield toward the Friendship Col trail and the hut.

name: Magog
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier.
[approach] Hike across the snowfield to the east face and cross the moat to rock below the notch between the two summits.
[descent_text] Cross the moat and walk back down the snowfield toward the hut.

name: Mount Quadrant West Face to North Summit (Stem-winder)
text: [overview] Snow may cover the approach and return.

[approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the Friendship Col trail until it turns up the snow slopes toward Gog and Magog, then continue straight over the ridge, drop down and around the left side of the lake, and climb back up to the base of Quadrant's north face.
[approach] There is some snow on the approach.

name: Another Fine Day in The Bugaboos
text: [overview] After a short moat pitch, pitches 1 to 3 (5.7) trend through cracks and corners beside a gendarme.
[approach] Cross snow and scree beneath the east buttress of Brenta Spire toward its northeast spur;
[approach] the route begins from the snow in a moat at the foot of that spur.
[descent_text] a short scramble and a final rappel lead into a moat, so an ice axe is useful.

name: Seppuku
text: [overview] wet in early season from snowmelt.
[approach] Follow the Sky Pilot approach to the Stadium Glacier and traverse west toward Copilot.

name: West Ridge
text: [approach] Follow the normal Sky Pilot approach up to the Stadium Glacier, then cross easy snow slopes west to the foot of Copilot.
[approach] Leave the snow and scramble up to the start of a corner, which is where the climbing begins;

name: Energy Crisis
text: [approach] Pass the first lake on its west side and the second on its east side, then continue straight north up the Crescent Glacier to the south face of the spire.
[approach] Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier.

name: McTech Arete
text: [approach] Pass the first lake on its west side and the second on its east side, then continue straight north up the Crescent Glacier to the south face of the spire.
[approach] Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier.
[approach] The route starts off the same large ledge as Paddle Flake, a short scramble above the glacier, but a bit farther right, from a big boulder below a set of flakes.

name: Paddle Flake
text: [approach] Pass the first lake on its west side and the second on its east side, then continue straight north up the Crescent Glacier to the south face of the spire.
[approach] Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier.
[approach] Scramble up from the glacier onto the large ledge that the McTech Arete route also starts from, and follow it left past that route to the start.

name: Paddle Flake Direct
text: [approach] Pass the first lake on its west side and the second on its east side, then continue straight north up the Crescent Glacier to the south face of the spire.
[approach] Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier.
[approach] Scramble up from the glacier onto a large ledge and follow it left to the start, which is left of McTech Arete and just left of a big left-facing dihedral.

name: Ears Between
text: [approach] From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground and head for the foot of the wall, following faint paths through boulders and past what is left of the Crescent Glacier.

name: Eternal Darkness
text: [overview] Descent: four 60 m rappels, starting slightly skiers left of the summit, reach a snow and dirt gully;
[descent_text] Further rappels lead into the snow and dirt gully, which can be walked down and circled back under the face to the start.

name: Phillips Ridge Route
text: [beta] Cross to Moraine Lake, climb the south and southeast scree slopes toward the north end of the summit ridge, and ascend the steep couloir (roughly 55 degrees in places, with a narrow line beside the snow).
[hazards] Steep snow couloir with a no-fall runout.
[gear] Ice axe.
[gear] Crampons.
[turnaround] Turn back if the couloir snow is not firm or if rockfall is active above you;
[pitch_detail] Steep snow in a couloir, then about 50 m of scrambling on loose basalt..
[pro_tips] Carry an ice axe and crampons in early season.

name: Gnomon Direct
text: [approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.

[descent_text] From the notch you can escape down the couloir behind it, using a mix of rappels and down-climbing on steep snow and ice, or climb one more long, easier pitch to the rim of the summit plateau and descend from there to the left (north) into the major couloir be
[descent_text] An ice axe and crampons are almost always needed, and anchors may need backing up or replacing, so carry rappel webbing and a few pitons.

name: Kiss of Death (Sinnes Couloir)
text: [detailed_rack] Conditions are steep snow or neve, with no ice.
[approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.

name: Lillarete
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — nearly always needed
[approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.
[approach] From the bivy area, cross the snow to the face of the Randy Stoltmann Buttress and start to the left of the prominent chimney that splits the face, beginning with a flake against the wall.

[descent_text] From the notch you can escape down the couloir behind it, using a mix of rappels and down-climbing on steep snow and ice, or climb one more long, easier pitch to the rim of the summit plateau and descend from there to the left (north) into the major couloir be
[descent_text] An ice axe and crampons are almost always needed, and anchors may need backing up or replacing, so carry rappel webbing and a few pitons.
